properties.name: Skills are composed of attribute classes, and the composition found its own miscast class
properties.rationale:
⭐ THE MECHANISM PROVED ITSELF BY BEING WRONG, TWICE, AND THAT IS THE RECORD WORTH KEEPING.

FIRST, THE CLASS WAS MISCAST. Charging all 18 writers with "search before creating" produced 11 failures — but `genesis` runs on an EMPTY GRAPH by definition, `impact-check` records a ChangeEvent which is new by nature, and `parallel-work` records a claim. Those were not omissions; the class was too coarse. Splitting MINTS out of WRITES cut the list to 14, every one real. **The refinement came from RUNNING it, not from thinking harder before writing it** — which is the argument for construction over inspection, arriving from inside the thing being built.

SECOND, THE OBLIGATIONS WERE LITERAL PHRASES and 13 of the 29 first-run failures were matching artifacts rather than deficiencies. `OPTIMIZE_CONTRACT`'s own comment had predicted exactly this and the warning was in the file being edited. The trap then bit a THIRD time during the fix: new `impact-check` text wrapped "could not\nestablish" across a newline and failed for the documented reason. The line was reflowed; the check was not weakened. The governing rule is now written beside the classes — ADDING A PHRASING FOR THE SAME OBLIGATION IS LEGITIMATE, REMOVING THE OBLIGATION IS NOT.

⭐ WHAT IT FOUND, which is the payoff Anthony asked for: EIGHT skills that mint concept nodes never said to search first — a mechanic `capture-intent` and `brainstorm` both carry. Nobody had noticed because until now nothing could ask a per-class question. That is "a successful skill does something the others do not", surfaced automatically rather than discovered by accident.

📌 AND THE SECOND REASON IS CREDIBILITY, NOT MAINTENANCE. Anthony: *"having reflow2 reflect all the principles it says it will do for other projects is not necessarily a functional win, but it is a 'marketing' win in terms that reflow2 'looks the part'."* It is stronger than that: `dec:mosa-conformance` asks whether reflow2 should report MOSA conformance for other people's designs, and its own skill surface would have failed the severability criterion — three contracts that cannot be composed, applied selectively, or replaced independently.

⚠️ ORDER HELD, and it is the one that bit earlier in the same session: both frontmatter parsers were checked to tolerate unknown keys BEFORE 69 files were edited, and `cargo fmt --check` ran before any baseline was taken.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `composes: [...]` added to the frontmatter of all 23 served skills across all three trees, plus a CLASSES table in `skill_lint.py` that checks each skill only against the classes it declares. Seven classes: STANDING, WRITES, MINTS, REVISES, REPORTS, MEASURES, DESTROYS. Fourteen real omissions found and fixed with prose written per skill.
